$comment: Kurultay user configuration template. Copy it to ~/.kurultay/config.json (Windows: C:\Users\<you>\.kurultay\config.json); it is used by every project. Replace every value written as <...>; Kurultay names the ones still left when it starts. A section you do not use (jira, gitlab, helper) can be deleted. A value written as ${NAME} is read from the environment variable NAME (e.g. "token": "${JIRA_TOKEN}"), so passwords and keys can stay out of the file.
baseUrl: <address of your LLM server, ending in /v1 – e.g. http://10.0.0.5:8000/v1>
apiKey: <API key of the LLM server – none if it needs no key>
models: <first model name as the server lists it – e.g. qwen3-coder-30b>
<second model (optional: delete this line if there is only one)>

helper.$comment: Optional: a small model that only writes summaries. Delete the whole section if you have none.
helper.baseUrl: <address of the small model's server – e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1>

verify.$comment: Build and test commands, run after every change. Leave empty when the project builds only in an IDE; a project's own kurultay.config.json can set them per project.

jira.$comment: Only for 'kurultay jira': issues assigned to you that mention @kurultay. Server/Data Center: a personal access token (Profile → Personal Access Tokens) in token; or username + password. Cloud: your e-mail in username and an API token in token.

gitlab.$comment: The repository the Jira work is done in – optional when every issue names its own with @kurultay{repo:<url>} in the description (then delete the repo line). token: a GitLab personal access token with scope 'api' (opens the merge request); targetBranch empty = the default branch.
